rationale: The workflow already implements concurrency cancellation with cancel-in-progress: true (addressing P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) and a job timeout of 120 minutes (addressing P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT). It is a single job with no matrix, so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST does not apply. There is no Bazel build, so P-LIT-BAZEL-* patterns do not apply. The workflow does not install pip/npm dependencies itself; it downloads and runs an external build script, so dependency-cache patterns (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE, P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE) have no applicable installation step to cache and the S3 script download is a small, versioned artifact where caching could introduce stale-content risk. There are no scheduled runs, so schedule-related patterns do not apply. Build/test selection and prioritization patterns cannot be applied at the workflow level because execution is delegated to an external script whose internals are not visible in the workflow. No supported evidence-backed optimization fits this workflow without weakening coverage or making unsupported assumptions.
